results.name: the-importance-of-hot-summers-and-individual-heatwaves-for-permafrost-warming-an
results.notes: This dataset contains idealized sensitivity simulations performed with the SNOWPACK model to investigate how the timing of summer heat affects ground thermal conditions in alpine permafrost. The simulations demonstrate that late-summer heatwaves lead to greater heat retention in the ground until the following spring than equally warm early-summer events. The dataset supports analyses of the influence of atmospheric heat timing on active-layer heat storage and permafrost thermal evolution.

organization.name: cryos
organization.title: CRYOS
organization.description:
CRYOS is the EPFL laboratory of the WSL/SLF - EPFL joint appointment for Prof. Michael Lehning. At his WSL side, Prof. Michael Lehning is head of the research unit "Snow and Permafrost" at SLF in Davos.
 
###General Mission
The laboratory of cryospheric sciences investigates the processes that shape snow and ice in mountains and polar regions. In particular, snow cover processes, snow-atmosphere interactions and mountain hydrology are in the focus of current research. This includes a strive for deeper understanding of the complicated mass and energy exchange processes within, above and below a snow cover but also predictions of future snow and ice in mountains and high latitudes. A newer work area is the risk management and optimization in the field of renewable energy production based on our detailed understanding of water, wind and radiation processes in mountains.

More information: http://cryos.epfl.ch/

results.name: dataset-for-canopy-scale-vpd-reduction-in-a-mature-forest-alters-stomatal-respon
results.notes:
This is the dataset used to generate the analyses (statistical tests and figures) for the article "Canopy-scale VPD reduction in a mature forest alters stomatal response to soil drought in Pinus sylvestris L.".
The data are already filtered as specified in the material and method sections of the related article.

organization.name: functional-plant-ecology
organization.title: Functional Plant Ecology
organization.description:
Our research group aims to better understand the physiological and ecological responses of terrestrial ecosystems to global change, with a focus on anticipating and counteracting its effects.

Our key research themes are the impact of biodiversity loss on ecosystem functions and services, as well as the physiological processes of plant responses to climatic constraints such as drought and increasing temperatures and VPD.

We use novel techniques and approaches at scales going from the cell to the whole ecosystem in diverse environmental conditions in temperate, Mediterranean and tropical systems. We conduct research in controlled conditions (e.g., greenhouses and growth chambers), in manipulative experiments in natural ecosystems (e.g., drought and temperature manipulation) and use long-term national and international inventory platforms. 

This integrative approach has both theoretical and applied aims to address the parameterization of climate-vegetation models and guide new climate-smart management practices.

results.title: Dataset for "Canopy-scale VPD reduction in a mature forest alters stomatal response to soil drought in Pinus sylvestris L."

resources.description: Whole plant physiological data collected at 60' resolution in individual trees (indicated with tree_number, scaffold and treatment): GS (whole-plant canopy conductance), E (whole-plant transpiration), TWDnorm ( normalized tree water deficit), pump_active (TRUE or FALSE, indicates if the VPD reduction system was active or not), max_wp (daily pre-dawn water potential computed with TWDnorm interpolation), tot_fl (total sap flow), crown_area_full (projected canopy area), and the corresponding environmental variables (VPD, PPFD, RH, Tair, soil mp) for the same timestamp.
resources.name: file2_physiological_60min.csv

resources.description: leaf level gas exchange data collected during monthly campaigns at the tree individual level (identified by their number, scaffold number, treatment), for every record: VPD (kPa), stomatal conductance gs (mol m-2 s-1), CO2 assimilation (umol m-2 s-1), PPFD (umol m-2 s-1), transpiration (mol m-2 s-1)
resources.name: file4_leaf_gas_exchange.csv

resources.description: environmental data collected at 10' resolution at the different experimental plots, indicated with the scaffold_n and treatment: VPD (kPa), PPFD (umol m-2 s-1), RH (%), Tair (°C), soil mp at -80cm (kPa), soil mp at -120cm (kPa).
resources.name: file1_environmental_10min.csv

resources.description: leaf water potential data (bar) collected during monthly campaigns at the tree individual level
